note: The C shape of CAGED: open C fretted with fingers 2, 3 and 4 (its chord box pinned, so it stays the open shape), the same shape two frets up with its arpeggio, major pentatonic and major scale, then joined to the A shape on the A string root. The old Key selector is now moves (any key), so the text names the key only as {{=key}} and a {{?key}} line says what stays the same; each block has one feel to reach.

exercise.title: CAGED: the C shape
exercise.why: The open C chord moves up the neck like E and A do, with finger 1 across the top three strings in place of the nut, and it ends on the A string where the A shape of the same chord begins.

cells.text: Press the chord box below to hear C. Fret it as shown, but with fingers 2, 3 and 4, so finger 1 is free.

Press Play on the chord panel below to hear {{=key}} in the C shape: the open C shape moved up the neck, with finger 1 lying across the top three strings in place of the nut. Then press Play on the other three panels: the arpeggio, the {{=key}} major pentatonic scale and the {{=key}} major scale sit in the same frets.
Play each one on your guitar, starting and ending on a root.
Practice until you can see the chord inside the scale.

Press Play on the two chord panels below to hear {{=key}} in the C shape, then in the A shape just above it. Play one, then the other, on your guitar: the root on the A string is the same note in both, and that is where the two shapes join.
Practice until your hand finds that root from either shape.
{{?key}}In another key both shapes move along the neck and still join on the A string.
